title: Predictive degradation orchestrator for multi-region KV and stream dependencies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During cross-region surges we observe correlated tail-latency spikes from Redis and Kafka tiers that cascade into request timeouts and tenant-visible errors. Existing connection pool trimming and simple circuit breakers either overreact (dropping useful traffic) or underreact (allowing saturation). Goal: build a predictive degradation orchestrator that scores incoming requests by utility and risk, orchestrates region-aware admission control, triggers graded circuit actions for downstream backends (Redis/Kafka/SQL), and exposes safe escape hatches for high-priority tenants. The orchestrator should be runtime light, compatible with Dedicated and Hosted modes, and integrate with Console for visibility and manual overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Component can attach to front-tier proxy and score incoming requests using a lightweight heuristic (latency history, tenant priority, request type) with <2ms median overhead

When a downstream (e.g., Redis primary in us-east) exceeds configured error/latency thresholds, orchestrator can: (a) reroute low-utility requests to cached responses or stale-read proxies; (b) reject or shed low-priority requests with clear 429+Retry-After; (c) open scoped circuit breakers and notify Console
Multi-region failover policy exercises a warm standby replica pool and confirms correctness via synthetic probe (success within 3s for auth+basic read path) before routing production traffic
System exposes per-tenant metrics (admissions, rejections, degraded percentage) and alerting for >1% user-impact within 5m window
Feature can be toggled and configured via Console rollout rules and supports per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private
implementation_plan: Design phase: define request utility score and risk model (inputs: tenant tier, route type, KV hit rate, recent downstream error budget) - document algorithm and edge cases
Prototype: implement scoring and admission in a sidecar filter for front proxy (Envoy/Wasm) with an in-memory sliding window for recent downstream signals
Connector adapters: create small connectors that translate downstream health signals (Redis latency P95/P99, Kafka consumer lag, DB connection queue depth) into normalized risk metrics

Circuit actions: implement staged actions: 1) soft-mark (add header to force cache hit), 2) priority-lane admission, 3) reject with structured payload, 4) full circuit open with fallback model variant
Observability: emit structured events to Console and trace sampling for graded-degradation decisions; create default dashboards and SLO-based alerts
Chaos & test: run in shadow mode for 2 weeks, then staged canary (10% of traffic), then ramp based on stability and metric pass criteria
rollout_plan: 1) Shadow run (2 weeks) with admin-only console to review decisions. 2) Canary at 10% in non-critical region (EU) for 72 hours. 3) Incremental region rollouts with emergency kill switch. 4) Enable per-customer require-approval flow for Dedicated customers. Communication: release notes, runbook, postmortem template. Backout: immediate disable flag and gradual rollback if >0.5% new customer errors or >25% increase in host CPU.
monitoring_and_metrics: SLO burn rate for critical endpoints (alerts when >2x burn)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Scoring may misclassify rarely-used critical requests -> Mitigation: safe-list routes and require per-route policy opt-ins
Risk: Orchestrator becomes a single point of failure -> Mitigation: lightweight fail-open mode where decisions degrade to conservative defaults and health-check autopass
Risk: Observability blindspots during canary -> Mitigation: add focused synthetic probes and end-to-end canary tracing before moving to broad rollout
Risk: Tenant dissatisfaction if aggressive shedding affects paying customers -> Mitigation: per-tenant policy with guaranteed minimum QPS, and pre-approved high-priority lanes
notes: Key design trade-offs: keep scoring model simple and explainable (deterministic heuristics) for first iteration; plan ML-based scoring in a follow-up only if error classification shows >15% false positives. Runtime targets: <2ms median decision time, <1% additional p95 latency on front tier. Integration: work with Console team for UI controls and with CI infra to add chaos tests to nightly suites.
